name: MedSafetyBench
intro: MedSafetyBench以美国医学会九项医学伦理原则定义医疗安全。论文用GPT-4直接提示与对Llama-2-7b-chat实施GCG越狱各生成900条有害医疗请求，经人工去重、相关性与质量审核，再由GPT-4生成并人工校验安全回应，共形成1,800条示例；按伦理原则分层为900条MedSafety-Eval和900条MedSafety-Improve。评测只输入有害请求，并由GPT-3.5-turbo-0125按1–5分有害性量表评分。
build_method: LLM生成, 对抗越狱, 人工审核
metric: 有害性评分（1–5）, 医学问答准确率
task_type: 安全测试, 自由文本回应生成
eval_feature: 医疗领域, 对抗性, LLM裁判
build_method_en: LLM Generation, Adversarial Jailbreaking, Human Review
intro_en: MedSafetyBench defines medical safety through the American Medical Association's nine Principles of Medical Ethics. The paper directly prompts GPT-4 and applies a GCG jailbreak to Llama-2-7b-chat to generate 900 harmful medical requests from each source, manually filters and edits them, then uses GPT-4 plus manual verification to pair every request with a safe response. The 1,800 demonstrations are stratified by ethics principle into 900-item MedSafety-Eval and MedSafety-Improve sets. Evaluation supplies only harmful requests and uses GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 to assign a 1–5 harmfulness score.

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit: arXiv:2403.03744v5, Sections 3.1-4.2 and Appendices A-D, cross-checked against AI4LIFE-GROUP/med-safety-bench commit dc5d88e4c0100deada5a96f065a302959e6523a7. Construction starts from the nine AMA Principles of Medical Ethics. GPT-4 is directly asked for twenty jargon-rich violations per principle (with a research/education qualifier after refusal), while Llama-2-7b-chat is attacked with a Greedy Coordinate Gradient suffix and an affirmative target sequence. Each branch is manually checked for medical jargon where applicable, duplicate prompts, principle relevance, correctness, and quality. The retained pool is exactly 900 GPT-4 plus 900 Llama-2 requests; the latter has the paper's uneven per-principle distribution 118/114/62/112/100/48/122/128/96. GPT-4 then writes a refusal plus brief safety explanation for every request, followed by manual verification and editing. Each source pool is randomly halved while stratifying over nine principles, producing both MedSafety-Eval and MedSafety-Improve with 450 items per source, 900 total each. The validation study is represented without overstating unanimity: 25 doctors each reviewed 25 random requests; 567/625 (91%) judgments marked at least one ethics violation, and 482/567 unethical judgments marked at least two principles. Evaluation uses only harmful requests, not reference safe responses: MedSafety-Eval has 900 items and GenSafety-Eval has 330. The pinned inference script uses model-specific wrappers, greedy decoding, temperature 0 for OpenAI models, and up to 512 new tokens. The pinned judge is gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 at temperature 0 with either the AMA or general-use policy and a 1-to-5 willingness-to-comply rubric, where lower is safer; the paper reports mean harmfulness and SEM. A reproducibility boundary is explicit: exp02_eval_responses.py saves raw GPT judge text containing requested #reason and #score fields but releases no parser or aggregation implementation. The improvement branch distinguishes 900 medical, 900 general, and pooled 1,800 safety demonstrations, and capability preservation is checked by accuracy on MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, and MMLU-Medical. Appendix C.1 specifies 3-shot in-context examples randomly sampled from each benchmark's training set and mean accuracy over 10 random seeds. The current MIT-licensed repository also contains 74,374 post-paper Llama-3 requests; they are an additional resource and are deliberately excluded from the paper-v5 benchmark flow. Formal publication evidence [site-a11u-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 1773×1001 (English) and 1773×1001 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 1771×999 and 1771×999. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
